newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges UN envoy not to bow to U.S. pressure.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges UN envoy not to bow to U.S. pressure.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra on Monday urged newly appointed United Nations arms envoy Richard Butler not to bow to U.S. and Kuwaiti pressure concerning Iraq's prohibited weapons.

The paper said Butler, chairman of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of destroying Iraq's prohibited weapons, "should be cautioned, accurate and objective toward any thing comes from American and Kuwaiti sources concerning Iraq."

Butler, who replaced Sweden's Rolf Ekeus on July 1, ended last week a five-day visit to Iraq. He then said he had agreed with the Iraqis on a plan for the next month to eradicate biological, chemical and missile weapons.
After his visit to Iraq, Butler flew to Kuwait to hear the views and concerns of the Kuwaiti leadership.

"If the commission wants to be really objective, Butler should know that there are two states which are keen to escalate tension between Iraq and the commission; they are America and Kuwait," Thawra said in a front-page editorial.
The paper said Butler was quoted as saying he wanted to start a new phase with Iraq and be objective in his assassment of Iraq's weapons.
"Statements are not the decisive factor to shape up the atmposphere (relations) between Iraq and the Special Commission, rather it is practical stands," Thwara said.

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations can lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, although Baghdad is allowed limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
"We would like to help him (Butler) achieve his mission (in Iraq) in the nearest time possible," the paper said.
